trajectory_summary: The agent loaded and inspected the TESS lightcurve, confirmed all quality flags were good, removed outliers, and detrended the strong stellar-variability signal using lightkurve.flatten with multiple window lengths (Turns 1–4). It then searched for transit periodicities using both TransitLeastSquares and astropy BoxLeastSquares, repeatedly finding a strong signal near ~1.398 d and a related signal near ~2.798 d (Turns 3–10). It performed an odd/even transit-depth consistency check that favored ~2.799 d as the true orbital period over the ~1.398 d half-period alias (Turn 13). However, in the final steps it refined the BLS best period around ~1.39825 d (Turn 16) and wrote 1.39825 to /root/period.txt (Turn 17), then returned 1.39825 as the final answer (Turn 18).
what_worked: Data filtering/outlier removal and detrending were executed and evidenced repeatedly; e.g., Turn 16 shows: "lc=lk.LightCurve(...).remove_outliers(sigma=10)" followed by "lc=lc.flatten(window_length=wl, ...).remove_outliers(sigma=6)".
Period search was performed with BoxLeastSquares and refined on a dense grid; Turn 16 reports "refined best (likelihood) 1.398247932452536".
The required output file was created with the requested formatting; Turn 17 wrote to /root/period.txt and printed "wrote 1.39825".
A diagnostic to distinguish half-period aliases from true periods was implemented earlier; Turn 13 compared P vs 2P and found odd/even consistency strongly favored the doubled period.

issues.evidence: Turn 13: the agent’s own BLS odd/even test favored ~2P: "at ~2P=2.79879348 d ... odd-even fraction ~-0.00384 (consistent odd/even depths), favoring the ~2.799 d interpretation as the true orbital period." Yet Turn 16 refined and Turn 17/18 reported and wrote "1.39825" as the final orbital period.
issues.cause: The agent failed to carry forward its own validation that the ~1.398 d peak was a half-period alias and instead selected the highest BLS peak (which can prefer the half-period when primary/secondary or odd/even effects exist) without reapplying the odd/even consistency criterion at the final selection step.

issues.evidence: The refinement explicitly optimized only around the single best coarse BLS peak: "coarse best (likelihood) 1.3982309087784257" then refined within +/-0.2% of that value, never evaluating the corresponding doubled period (~2.7965–2.7988 d) under the same objective.
issues.cause: Narrow refinement around the strongest peak can lock in an alias if the global optimum corresponds to a harmonic; a robust approach would also test 2P (and possibly P/2) with consistency checks (odd/even, secondary eclipse, transit shape) before finalizing.

outcome_rationale: Although the period was successfully written to /root/period.txt, the final reported value (1.39825 d) conflicts with the agent’s own earlier odd/even validation favoring ~2.799 d as the true orbital period, making the delivered orbital period likely incorrect.
